prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that periodically reads moisture levels from a DFRobot Soil Moisture Sensor v2.0, an analog resistive sensor, via an MCP3008 analog-to-digital converter connected over the SPI bus. Wire the MCP3008 to the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus: chip enable CE0 on GPIO8, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, and SCLK on GPIO11, with the sensor's analog output wired to MCP3008 channel 0 (CH0). Use the pigpio library for all SPI communication with the ADC. Sample the raw 10-bit ADC value, in the range 0-1023, once per second, and log each reading to the console together with a timestamp so the moisture trend can be reviewed later. Implement robust error handling around SPI initialization and every SPI transfer, reporting any failure rather than silently continuing. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for a graceful shutdown, making sure the SPI handle is closed and pigpio is terminated cleanly on every exit path, including early failures.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that reads current from an MLX91219 Hall-effect current sensor, which has an analog output, via an ADS1115 analog-to-digital converter over I2C, using the pigpio library for all I2C communication. Wire the ADS1115's ADDR pin to GND, giving it I2C address 0x48 on bus 1; wire the MLX91219's analog output to the ADS1115's AIN0 input; and wire the ADS1115's SDA and SCL lines to the Pi's GPIO2 and GPIO3. Configure the ADS1115 for single-shot mode, AIN0 single-ended (MUX=100), a programmable gain amplifier setting of PGA ±4.096V, and a data rate of 128 samples per second. Every 500ms, log the computed current in amperes to the console, deriving it from the MLX91219's sensitivity of 40mV/A with its zero-current offset centered at mid-supply. Access the ADS1115's 16-bit registers with i2cWriteI2CBlockData and i2cReadI2CBlockData, respecting the correct byte order, and handle I2C write and read errors as well as sensor-absent paths gracefully rather than crashing. On SIGINT, close the I2C handle and call gpioTerminate() before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with an AZDelivery KY-026 Flame Sensor Module and an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, using the pigpio library only (do not use wiringPi). Read the KY-026 digital output (D0) on GPIO4 (BCM numbering) and sample its analog output (A0) on MCP3008 channel 0 (single-ended); connect the MCP3008 to SPI0 (CE0/GPIO8) at 1 MHz. Approximate ambient temperature from the analog reading using a linear map of the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to 10-40°C. Once per second, log timestamped CSV rows (Timestamp,FlameDetected,Temperature) to flame_data.csv. Implement robust error handling: verify pigpio initialization, SPI open/transfer, and file operations; on sensor-absent or SPI-failure paths, skip the log entry and print a diagnostic. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including SIGINT.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that monitors two sensors and activates a buzzer when both indicate a fire condition simultaneously, using the pigpio library for all GPIO and I2C access. Connect a Keyes KY-026 Flame Sensor's digital output to GPIO4, using the internal pull-up resistor; the sensor outputs LOW when a flame is detected. Connect an LM393-based Heat Sensor's analog output to an ADS1115 ADC on I2C bus 1 at address 0x48, channel AIN0 (single-ended), configured for single-shot mode, gain ±4.096V, 128 SPS (conversion time ~8.5ms); map the ADC voltage range 0V-3.3V linearly to 20°C-80°C and treat above 60°C as a trigger. Connect the buzzer to GPIO27, active HIGH. Poll the flame sensor and read the temperature every 100ms. Implement a 50ms debounce on the flame sensor using a falling-edge ISR callback, registering a flame event only if at least 50ms have elapsed since the last accepted event. If both a debounced flame event and temperature above 60°C occur together, log the event with a timestamp to fire_log.txt and sound the buzzer for 2 seconds. If only flame is detected, log "Flame detected!"; if only the temperature exceeds 60°C, log the temperature reading. If the ADC read fails (I2C error or sensor absent), log an error and continue without crashing. Check the return values of pigpio initialization, I2C open, the ADC configuration write, the ADC read, and log file creation, printing descriptive errors to stderr for each failure path; on any initialization failure, release all resources acquired so far and exit with code 1. Handle SIGINT by setting a running flag to 0 so the main loop exits cleanly, then turn off the buzzer, deregister the ISR, close the I2C handle, close the log file, and call gpioTerminate(). Use only pigpio, never wiringPi or libgpiod; drive the buzzer with a simple digital write rather than PWM; and ensure the code compiles cleanly with gcc -Wall, with no undeclared identifiers or implicit declarations.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 to interface with a Melexis MLX91219 current sensor (SOIC8 package, -40°C to 125°C range), which provides an analog output proportional to measured current. Read the analog signal via an external MCP3008 10-bit ADC (VREF = 3.3 V) on SPI0 CE0 (spidev0.0, GPIO8, SPI channel 0) at 1 MHz, SPI mode 0, 8 bits per word, using spidev for SPI access; read single-ended channel 0 with the 3-byte SPI command (0x01, 0x80, 0x00) and extract the 10-bit result as ((rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | rx[2]. Convert the ADC voltage to current using the sensor sensitivity (default 100 mV/A, configurable via -s). If the measured current exceeds a configurable threshold (default 5.0 A, configurable via -t), drive GPIO18 HIGH to turn on a cooling fan; otherwise drive it LOW. Sample once per second and log every reading with an ISO-8601 timestamp to current_log.txt. Use libgpiod for all GPIO control, never sysfs or wiringPi, opening the GPIO chip by name (try "gpiochip4" for Pi 5, falling back to chip 0). Implement robust error handling: check every open/ioctl/read/write call, handle SPI transfer failures, and handle sensor-absent conditions where the ADC reads all-zero or all-ones. Ensure clean resource release on SIGINT/SIGTERM by closing the SPI file descriptor, releasing the GPIO lines, and turning the fan OFF. Include all necessary standard headers, such as stdint.h, so the code compiles cleanly.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an SGX Sensortech / Honeywell MICROceL MICS-4514 CO sensor, a dual-element MOS sensor (NO2 and CO) that outputs raw analog resistance values, using the pigpio library over I2C bus 1 at device address 0x28. Since the Raspberry Pi has no direct analog inputs, read the sensor via an external 16-bit ADC such as an ADS1115 over I2C, or simulate the raw 16-bit ADC readings for the CO element. Every 5 seconds, read the raw 16-bit CO resistance value, convert it to a CO concentration in PPM using a calibrated logarithmic curve, and log the timestamped PPM value to co_log.txt. Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, I2C handle creation, and I2C read failures such as a sensor-absent condition or bus errors. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including graceful shutdown on SIGINT and SIGTERM. Do not use the deprecated wiringPi library.

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with an AZDelivery KY-026 Flame Sensor Module and an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, using the pigpio library for all GPIO and SPI operations (do not use wiringPi). Connect the KY-026 digital output (D0) to GPIO4 and its analog output (A0) to MCP3008 channel 0. Connect the MCP3008 to the primary SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, SCLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9) with a 1 MHz SPI clock. Once per second, log the flame presence (1 = detected, 0 = no flame) and the ambient temperature, approximated via linear scaling of the 10-bit ADC value to 10.0-40.0°C, to a timestamped CSV file named flame_data.csv. Implement robust error handling: validate pigpio initialization, SPI handle creation, SPI transfer success, and file I/O; on sensor-absent or SPI bus-error paths, skip the log entry and print a diagnostic to stderr. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including SIGINT (Ctrl+C) signal handling.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an SGX Sensortech MICS-4514 dual MOS sensor (CO/NO2) via I2C using the pigpio library. The sensor provides two 16-bit ADC readings (OX for CO, RED for NO2) over 4 bytes. Every 5 seconds, read and calculate the CO level in PPM and log it to co_log.txt. Simulate an industrial air quality monitoring system with a 25 PPM alert threshold, logging alerts to alert_log.txt. Implement robust error handling for I2C initialization, read failures, and file I/O. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including signal handling for SIGINT and SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read sound pressure levels from two STMicroelectronics IMP23ABSU analog MEMS microphones and log the timestamped average to audio_log.txt, simulating a basic acoustic leak detection system. Since the IMP23ABSU is an analog microphone, connect its analog OUT pins to the Pi's I2C bus pins (GPIO2/BCM2 and GPIO3/BCM3) and read them using the pigpio library's I2C interface as a bit-banged ADC emulation, opening I2C bus 1 at addresses 0x48 and 0x49 and reading 2 bytes from register 0x00 of each. Sample every 100ms. Convert the 16-bit signed raw data to sound pressure level in dB using a microphone sensitivity of -38 dBV/Pa and a reference pressure of 20e-6 Pa. If either sensor read fails, log an error value of -999.0 dB and continue running. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for graceful shutdown, closing all I2C handles and terminating pigpio cleanly.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to sample audio from two Analog Devices ADMP401 MEMS microphones. Since the ADMP401 provides an analog output, feed each microphone's signal into an external MCP3008 ADC connected to the Pi's SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, CE1 on GPIO9, MISO on GPIO9, MOSI on GPIO10, SCLK on GPIO11), and use the pigpio library to read the ADC channels via SPI. Sample both microphone channels at a 1 ms interval for a 100 ms window (100 samples per channel) and calculate the RMS value for each channel. If the RMS value of either microphone exceeds a threshold of 0.7 of the normalized scale, turn on an LED connected to GPIO27 for 500 ms. Log every sampling window's timestamp, mic1 RMS, and mic2 RMS to a CSV file named audio_events.csv. Handle SPI initialization failures and file I/O errors, and exit gracefully on SIGINT (Ctrl+C), ensuring the LED is turned off and resources are released.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to sample the analog output of a Melexis MLX91204 Hall effect current sensor and simulate an overcurrent protection system, using the pigpio library. The MLX91204 provides a ratiometric analog voltage output of 0.5V to 4.5V for 0-100A, assuming a 5V supply. Since the Raspberry Pi lacks a built-in ADC, interface to an external ADS1115 ADC over I2C at address 0x48 (SDA=GPIO2, SCL=GPIO3, bus 1), reading single-ended on channel A0, using the pigpio I2C API functions i2cWriteDevice and i2cReadDevice for raw register operations. Continuously sample the sensor at 10Hz, log the converted current readings to a circular buffer of 100 elements, and trigger a warning LED on GPIO17 if the average current exceeds a threshold of 50.0A. Implement robust error handling for pigpio initialization, I2C bus reads, and sensor-absent conditions. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) for graceful shutdown, ensuring the LED is turned off and resources are released cleanly on all exit paths.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an Adafruit TCS34725 I2C color sensor (I2C address 0x29, bus 1) using the pigpio library for I2C (not wiringPi). Initialize pigpio and open the I2C bus, exiting with a non-zero error code if either fails. Verify the sensor is present by reading the ID register (0x12) and checking that the lower 4 bits equal 0x44; exit with an error if the ID does not match. Configure the sensor by setting the integration time (ATIME, register 0x01) to 0xFF (2.4 ms) and the gain (CONTROL, register 0x0F) to 0x01 (4x), then power on and enable the ADC (ENABLE, register 0x00 = 0x01 | 0x02), waiting at least 3 ms after power-on before reading. Every 1 second, read the 16-bit clear, red, green, and blue values from registers 0x14-0x1B and append a line to color_log.csv formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,clear,red,green,blue, writing a header row if the file is newly created. Check every I2C read/write return value; on a transient I2C read failure, print a warning to stderr and continue, and on 3 consecutive failures, exit gracefully. Install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler for clean shutdown that closes the I2C handle, flushes and closes the CSV file, and calls gpioTerminate(), and avoid blocking sleep calls that would prevent signal handling.

Because the Raspberry Pi has no built-in ADC, connect the sensors to an MCP3008 SPI ADC via the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, MISO on GPIO9, MOSI on GPIO10, SCLK on GPIO11), wiring the two sensors to MCP3008 channels 0 and 1. Use the modern libgpiod API, not sysfs or wiringPi, to control the MCP3008 chip-select line, and standard Linux spidev (/dev/spidev0.0) for SPI communication. Read both channels, map the raw 10-bit ADC values (0-1023) to a 0-100% moisture scale, and log timestamped readings to a CSV file named moisture_log.csv with header Timestamp,Moisture1,Moisture2. Sample every 5 seconds. Implement robust error handling: check all SPI and libgpiod initialization calls, handle sensor-absent or SPI bus-error paths gracefully, and ensure clean release of all resources, including SPI file descriptors and libgpiod lines, on all exit paths via SIGINT/SIGTERM signal handling.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Melexis MLX91211 Triaxis Current Sensor, logging current readings in Amperes to a comma-separated current_log.csv file, and simulating an overcurrent safety system for a DC motor. The MLX91211 is an analog ratiometric Hall-effect sensor, not an SPI device, so read it via an MCP3008 ADC connected over hardware SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8, SCLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9), with the sensor's analog output wired to MCP3008 channel 0. Use the modern libgpiod API for GPIO control and spidev for SPI communication with the MCP3008 (not bcm2835 or wiringPi). Sample the sensor every 1 second, convert the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to a voltage (0-3.3V), then to current using a sensitivity of 0.1 V/A and an offset of 0.05V. If the current exceeds 10.0A, drive a motor shutdown pin (GPIO17) LOW to disable the motor, log the event, wait 1 second, then drive it HIGH to re-enable. Check all open(), ioctl(), read(), and file I/O operations for errors, and retry SPI communication errors up to 3 times. Implement signal handling (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for graceful shutdown, closing all file descriptors and releasing GPIO lines cleanly on exit. Log each reading as timestamp,current_in_Amperes, writing the header if the file is new or empty.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to interface with a Melexis MLX90817 absolute pressure sensor over I2C bus 1 at 7-bit address 0x40, using the pigpio library for I2C. Once per second, read the 16-bit pressure value from register 0x00 and convert it to pressure in kPa using pressure_kPa = (raw_value / 65535.0) * 500.0. Log each reading with an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp to a comma-separated file named pressure_log.csv with columns timestamp,pressure_kPa, opening the file once at startup with a header row rather than on every write, and flushing after each write. Check every pigpio/I2C call and file operation for errors; on an I2C read failure, print an error to stderr with the register and the pigpio error code, and continue the loop without logging. Handle sensor-absent scenarios, including I2C open failure or repeated read failures. Install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler to cleanly close the I2C handle, flush and close the log file, and call gpioTerminate() before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Melexis MLX90834 pressure sensor. The MLX90834 is a SENT-only MEMS pressure sensor with no native I2C interface, so read its analog pressure output via a generic I2C ADC bridge, an ADS1115 at address 0x48, using the pigpio library for both I2C and GPIO. Configure the ADS1115 to read single-ended on AIN0 (pressure signal) and AIN1 (NTC temperature signal) at a gain of 2/3 (FSR ±6.144V), 128 SPS. Convert the ADC voltage to pressure using a linear transfer function (0V = 0 kPa, 5V = 400 kPa) and to temperature using a simplified linear NTC approximation (1V = 0°C, 2V = 100°C). Every 1 second, display the pressure (kPa) and temperature (°C) on the console, and drive a warning LED on GPIO17 (active-high) HIGH when pressure exceeds 105.0 kPa. Implement robust error handling: validate every pigpio call, retry failed I2C reads up to 3 times, and handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths. Ensure clean resource release on SIGINT.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that reads motor current using a Melexis MLX91209 Hall-effect current sensor (analog output) via an MCP3008 10-bit SPI ADC, using only the pigpio library (no wiringPi). Connect the MLX91209 analog output to MCP3008 channel 0 (single-ended), with the MCP3008 on SPI0 CE0 (GPIO8 CE, GPIO11 SCLK, GPIO10 MOSI, GPIO9 MISO) at 1 MHz, SPI mode 0. The MCP3008 protocol uses a 3-byte transfer: a start bit (0x01), a single-ended channel configuration byte, and a zero pad byte; extract the 10-bit result from the last two bytes of the response. Convert the 10-bit ADC reading to a voltage (0-3.3V full-scale, 1024 steps), then to current using the sensor's zero-current midpoint at Vcc/2 and a sensitivity of 66 mV/A. Sample every 100ms and log each reading with a timestamp to current_log.txt in append mode, flushing after every write. Implement a safety monitor: if current exceeds 10A, assert GPIO27 HIGH to trigger a motor shutdown, log an OVERCURRENT event, and stop the program. Handle all error paths: pigpio initialization failure, SPI open/transfer errors, invalid ADC values, and file I/O errors. On SIGINT/SIGTERM, cleanly close the SPI handle, close the log file, reset GPIO27 to LOW, and call gpioTerminate().

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with a Honeywell MICROceL MCO-S4 CO sensor whose analog voltage output is read via an external MCP3008 ADC connected to the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus (CE0 on BCM GPIO8, SCLK on BCM 11, MOSI on BCM 10, MISO on BCM 9), with the CO sensor's analog output wired to MCP3008 channel 0. Use the pigpio library, not wiringPi, to configure the SPI bus at 1 MHz (SPI mode 0) and to control an alarm on BCM GPIO4. Read the ADC continuously, once per second, convert the 10-bit ADC value to a voltage using a 3.3V reference, and drive the alarm on BCM GPIO4 HIGH if the voltage exceeds 2.5V, or LOW if it is 2.5V or below. Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to monitor methane levels with a Honeywell MICROpeL Model 41000-020 Combustible Gas Sensor (analog output) connected to an MCP3008 SPI ADC. Wire the MCP3008 as follows: VDD/VREF to Pi 3.3V (pin 1), DGND/AGND to Pi GND, CLK to GPIO11 (SCLK), DOUT to GPIO9 (MISO), DIN to GPIO10 (MOSI), CS/SHDN to GPIO8 (CE0), with the sensor's analog output feeding MCP3008 channel 0 (single-ended). Read the ADC once per second via SPI bus 0, channel 0, at 1 MHz, mode 0, using the MCP3008 3-byte SPI command sequence for single-ended channel 0 (start byte 0x01, config byte 0x80, dummy byte 0x00) and extracting the 10-bit result as ((rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | rx[2]. Convert the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to a methane concentration in PPM using linear scaling (0 -> 0 PPM, 1023 -> 5000 PPM). Log every reading with an ISO-8601 timestamp to methane_log.txt in append mode; if the concentration exceeds 1000 PPM, print a visible leak alarm to stderr. Implement robust error handling: check gpioInitialise(), spiOpen(), spiXfer(), fopen(), and localtime_r(); on an SPI transfer failure, log the error to stderr and continue rather than crash. Do not use wiringPi, and use pigpio's negative-handle error codes directly rather than calling gpioErrno.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read pressure data from a Melexis MLX90830 analog pressure sensor. Since the MLX90830 provides a ratiometric analog output, interface it via an external ADS1115 16-bit ADC at I2C address 0x48 on the Pi's I2C bus 1 (SDA=GPIO2, SCL=GPIO3), with the sensor's analog output connected to the ADS1115's AIN0 channel, using the pigpio library for I2C communication. Read the ADC at 1Hz, convert the raw value to a voltage, then to pressure in kPa using a linear transfer function assuming a 0.5V offset at 0 kPa and a sensitivity of 0.1 V/kPa. Implement robust error handling: check all I2C/ADC initialization and read operations, handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths, and validate the pressure range. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including graceful shutdown via SIGINT (Ctrl+C).

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with a Honeywell HIH-4602-A humidity sensor via SPI using the pigpio library. The HIH-4602-A provides an analog voltage output for relative humidity and contains an integral thermistor for temperature measurement; since the Raspberry Pi lacks analog inputs, use an external 12-bit MCP3208 ADC on SPI0 (CE0/GPIO8) to read both the humidity output and the thermistor voltage. Log readings to humidity_log.txt in comma-separated format (timestamp, humidity, temperature) with robust error handling for pigpio initialization, SPI transfer failures, and file I/O. prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 to read temperature data from a TMP36 analog temperature sensor via an external MCP3208 12-bit SPI ADC. Connect the TMP36 signal output to MCP3208 channel 0 (CH0, pin 1), and connect the MCP3208 SPI interface to the Pi 5's SPI0: CE0 (GPIO8), SCLK (GPIO11), MOSI (GPIO10), MISO (GPIO9), with the MCP3208's VDD and VREF tied to 3.3V. Use the modern libgpiod API, not sysfs or wiringPi, to manually control the MCP3208 CS line (GPIO8 on gpiochip4), and use spidev (/dev/spidev0.0) for SPI communication, configured for Mode 0, 8 bits per word, and 1 MHz max speed. Read the ADC at 1Hz, convert the 12-bit value (0-4095) to a voltage using VREF = 3.3V, then to Celsius using Temp = (Voltage - 0.5) / 0.01. Log each reading to a comma-separated temperature_log.csv file formatted as timestamp,temperature_celsius, writing the header only if the file is newly created. Implement robust error handling: check SPI open/ioctl/transfer operations, validate ADC readings, and handle sensor-absent or out-of-range conditions, such as a voltage outside the TMP36's valid range of -40C to 125C. Implement clean resource release on all exit paths, including signal handling for SIGINT and SIGTERM to gracefully close the SPI device, release GPIO lines, and close the log file.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an Analog Devices ADXL335 analog accelerometer via an MCP3008 10-bit ADC on SPI0, CE0/GPIO8, at 1 MHz, SPI Mode 0, using the pigpio library for SPI and GPIO. Connect the ADXL335 X/Y/Z outputs to MCP3008 channels 0/1/2. At 100 Hz, log the X, Y, Z raw ADC values to impact_log.txt, timestamped and comma-separated. Compute the acceleration magnitude in g using a 3.3V supply, with the ADXL335's 0g point at 1.65V and a sensitivity of 300 mV/g, and flag impacts exceeding 2.0g with an 'IMPACT DETECTED' line in the log. Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, SPI open, every spiXfer return value, and the file open call, and validate that ADC reads are within range. Handle SIGINT cleanly by closing SPI, closing the log file, and calling gpioTerminate. Ensure CS (GPIO8) is managed correctly around each SPI transfer.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read data from a Silicon Labs Si1172-A30-GMR Optical Heart Rate Sensor using I2C communication via the pigpio library (never wiringPi), on I2C bus 1 at the default 7-bit address 0x49. Log data to a comma-separated file named biometric_log.csv, with a header row, including a Unix timestamp, HR (bpm), SpO2 (%), and an error flag (0 = OK, 1 = read error, 2 = sensor absent/uninitialized). Sample once per second, flushing the file after each write, and handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) for graceful shutdown by closing the I2C handle, terminating pigpio, and closing the log file. Check the return value of every pigpio I2C call, distinguish between transient I2C errors and a completely absent sensor (an i2cOpen failure), and log an error row with the appropriate error flag when a read fails rather than crashing. Use the Si1172's command-based register access protocol: write the command register (0xC0) to trigger a measurement, then read the FIFO or data registers (0xC1-0xC4) for the raw photoplethysmography samples. Since the Si1172 requires a proprietary algorithm to convert raw PPG samples to HR/SpO2, read the raw 16-bit IR and RED ADC values from the FIFO and log those as proxy values for HR and SpO2 respectively, documenting this limitation in code comments.

Write a robust C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Honeywell SpiroQuant A+ ES1-005 Mass Flow Sensor for use in a portable oxygen concentrator monitoring system, using the pigpio library (SPI mode 0, 1 MHz baud, SPI channel 0 on CE0/GPIO8). The SpiroQuant A+ outputs an analog signal proportional to flow rate; since the Raspberry Pi lacks an ADC, read it via an external MCP3008 ADC over SPI and convert the value to flow rate using a linear scaling formula where 0-3.3V maps to 0-5.0 L/min. Log every 1 second with a microsecond-precision timestamp in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.uuuuuu,flow_rate to a comma-separated file named flow_log.csv, flushing after each write to ensure data integrity in a portable device. Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, SPI open, every SPI transfer, and the ADC read; handle sensor-absent conditions, where the ADC returns 0 or full-scale, and SPI bus-error paths. Validate that the flow rate is within the plausible range of 0.0 to 5.0 L/min, logging errors to stderr but continuing to run. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, with SIGINT/SIGTERM handling to close SPI, terminate pigpio, and close the file.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read temperature and pressure data from a TDK ICP-10125 I2C sensor using the Linux i2c-dev kernel interface (open/ioctl/read/write), not wiringPi. The sensor is connected to I2C bus 1 at address 0x67. Log timestamped readings to a comma-separated environmental_data.csv file and display the data on the console for real-time monitoring in a weather station prototype. Use the ICP-10125 measurement command 0x6845 to trigger a high-precision reading, wait for the conversion to finish, then read the 6-byte result (pressure MSB/LSB, temperature MSB/LSB, and CRC bytes). Apply the official ICP-10125 calibration formulas to convert the raw ADC values to temperature in °C and pressure in Pa. Implement robust error handling: check every I2C syscall (open, ioctl, write, read) and handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths by logging the error and retrying after 5 seconds. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths by closing the I2C file descriptor and the CSV log file, and use signal handling (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for graceful shutdown. Sample every 5 seconds.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that samples audio from two STMicroelectronics MP23ABS1 analog MEMS microphones using the pigpio library. Connect the microphones' analog outputs to an external MCP3008 ADC on the hardware SPI0 bus (CE0, GPIO8). Implement a basic noise-cancellation algorithm by subtracting the two audio streams, and output the resulting audio data to the terminal in CSV format. Implement a simple gain control via command-line arguments. Ensure robust error handling for pigpio initialization, SPI configuration, and sensor-absent/bus-error paths, and handle SIGINT for clean resource release on all exit paths.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Vegetronix VH400 soil moisture sensor using the pigpio library for SPI control. Connect the sensor's analog output to channel 0 (CH0) of an MCP3008 10-bit ADC, which communicates with the Pi over SPI0 (CE0). Log the moisture readings to a file named moisture_log.txt as comma-separated values of ISO 8601 UTC timestamps and raw 10-bit ADC readings (0-1023). Sample once every 60 seconds in an infinite loop. Implement robust error handling: check all pigpio initialization and SPI transfer calls, validate the ADC range, and handle file I/O errors gracefully. Ensure clean resource release on SIGINT/SIGTERM by closing the SPI handle and terminating the pigpio library.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read analog voltage values from a Keyes KY-026 Flame Sensor using an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, logging temperature-compensated voltage readings and a flame detection flag to flame_log.txt, and triggering a GPIO-based buzzer on flame detection, using the libgpiod C library (not wiringPi) for both GPIO buzzer control and SPI communication via /dev/spidev0.0. Configure the MCP3008 SPI link in mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0) at 1 MHz with a 3-byte transfer (start bit, single-ended config, dummy byte), extracting the 10-bit ADC value correctly. Read ambient temperature from a local file, ambient_temp.txt, falling back to 25.0°C if it is missing or invalid. Sample the sensor every 500ms. If the SPI transfer fails, log the error to stderr and the log file, skip the iteration, and turn the buzzer OFF for safety; if the ADC value is out of the 0-1023 range, retry up to 3 times before failing the iteration. Treat a compensated voltage above 1.0V as flame detected, computing it as voltage + (temperature - 25.0) * 0.001. Log each reading in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,raw_adc,voltage,compensated_voltage,temperature,flame_detected. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) gracefully: stop the loop, turn off the buzzer, close the log file, and release all libgpiod resources.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with a DFRobot Gravity Analog Water Level Sensor via an MCP3008 10-bit ADC, using the pigpio library for all GPIO and SPI operations (do not use wiringPi). Connect the MCP3008 to the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, MISO on GPIO9, MOSI on GPIO10, SCLK on GPIO11), and wire the water level sensor's analog output to MCP3008 channel 0. Initialize pigpio and open SPI channel 0 (CE0) at 1 MHz with SPI mode 0 (flags=0), checking all return codes and aborting gracefully on failure. Every 5 seconds, read the 10-bit ADC value from MCP3008 channel 0 using a 3-byte SPI transfer (start bit 0x01, config byte 0x80|channel<<4, padding 0x00; parse the result as ((rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | rx[2]), convert it to a percentage of the 0-1023 range, and print it to stdout. Log every reading to a JSON file named water_levels.json as a valid JSON array of objects, each containing an ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds and the water_level percentage; keep the file valid JSON even if the program is interrupted by opening with a '[' prefix, flushing after each entry, and closing with ']' on shutdown. Turn an LED connected to GPIO17 ON when the water level exceeds 75%, and OFF when it drops below 70% (hysteresis), driving it as a pigpio output. Handle SPI transfer errors (spiXfer returning less than 0) by logging the error via pigpio_error() and skipping that reading without crashing; use pigpio_error() for all pigpio error messages, not gpioErrText, and sleep in small increments (about 100ms via gpioDelay) so signals are handled promptly.

Write a robust C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read airflow data from an analog Honeywell AWM7300V mass airflow sensor via an external MCP3008 10-bit ADC, using the pigpio library. Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to monitor a potted plant using a HiLetgo Soil Moisture Sensor (analog resistive sensor) connected to an MCP3008 ADC, reading it via SPI using the pigpio library (never wiringPi). Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that continuously monitors soil moisture using a Keyes KY-036 analog sensor, using the pigpio library (not wiringPi). Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to periodically read analog data from a DFRobot Soil Moisture Sensor v2.0 connected to channel 0 (ADC0) of an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, using the modern libgpiod library to access the SPI device (/dev/spidev0.0) instead of the deprecated wiringPi library. Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the libgpiod library to periodically read analog data from a SEN0193 Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor connected to an MCP3008 ADC over SPI. Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit Bookworm, kernel 6.6+) using libgpiod to detect proximity via a GP2Y0A21YK0F Sharp IR distance sensor whose analog output is read through an ADS1115 ADC at I2C address 0x48 over /dev/i2c-1 using ioctl(I2C_SLAVE) and I2C_RDWR. Implement robust SPI communication error handling by validating the channel, checking the spiXfer return value, and detecting stuck or invalid ADC values, plus graceful GPIO initialization failure recovery. Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to read analog values from a YL-83 rain sensor whose analog output is wired to channel 0 (CH0) of an MCP3008 ADC on SPI0 (CE0, bus 0), with the MCP3008 VDD at 3.3 V so ADC full-scale = 1023, read in single-ended mode. Log each reading to stdout with a timestamp, the raw ADC value, and the intensity level. prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using the pigpio library to monitor an MQ-135 air quality sensor via an MCP3008 ADC connected over SPI (CE0, SPI0, Mode 0, 1 MHz), with the MQ-135 analog output on MCP3008 channel 0. Convert the 10-bit ADC reading to an approximate CO2 ppm value using a linear calibration (slope 0.5, intercept -50). When the estimated CO2 level exceeds 700 ppm, activate a ventilation fan connected to GPIO18 (HIGH = ON). Log every reading, sampled once every 5 seconds, to 'air_quality.log' in CSV format: timestamp,co2_ppm,fan_state. Handle SPI communication errors gracefully by logging and retrying rather than crashing, and validate ADC values against the 0-1023 range. Shut down cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM by turning off the fan, closing SPI, and releasing pigpio resources.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using libgpiod to monitor a GP2Y0A21YK0F IR distance sensor, read via an MCP3008 ADC on SPI0, CE0, channel 0, at a 1 MHz SPI clock, and control a 5V relay connected to a magnetic door sensor. When proximity is detected (< 20 cm), energize the relay, active-high on GPIO17, to simulate door opening. Use a 100 ms polling interval and a 1 s debounce delay after triggering. Log each event with a timestamp to 'door_events.log'. Include robust error handling for all GPIO, SPI, and file I/O operations, handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths, and cleanly release all resources on all exit paths, including SIGINT.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the pigpio library to control a proportional solenoid valve (ASCO RedHat 8210 series) connected to GPIO17 (PWM-capable, BCM numbering), modulating its opening based on readings from an analog soil moisture sensor (Vegetronix VH400) connected to an MCP3008 ADC via SPI channel 0 (CE0 on GPIO8), 1 MHz clock, SPI mode 0. Using pigpio's built-in SPI (spiOpen/spiXfer) with correct MCP3008 single-ended command bytes, read 3 sensors on ADC channels 0-2, average the readings, and map the average (0-1023) inversely to valve opening (0-100%): dry soil (low ADC value) gives high opening, wet soil (high ADC value) gives low opening. Set the PWM frequency to 100 Hz with range 100 for 0-100% duty cycle. Log the timestamp, the 3 raw ADC values, the average, and the valve position to 'irrigation.log' every 5 seconds. Check pigpio init, SPI open, every SPI transfer, and the log file open; handle individual sensor read failures by skipping them in the average. Use signal handlers (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for graceful shutdown: close the valve (PWM=0), close SPI, close the log file, and terminate pigpio.

Ensure the SPI command bytes are correctly formatted for the MCP3008 (start bit, single-ended mode, channel 0) and the 10-bit ADC value is extracted correctly; validate the ADC value against the 10-bit range (0-1023) before converting to a moisture percentage. Log readings with timestamps to 'soil_data.txt' every 5 seconds. Handle potential SPI communication errors gracefully with a retry mechanism of up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff; if SPI fails persistently, skip the reading and log an error. Implement graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM, ensuring all SPI handles and pigpio resources are released.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that synthesizes a Theremin-like instrument using libgpiod for GPIO control and the sysfs PWM interface (/sys/class/pwm/) for audio generation. Map the distance reading from a single HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor (Trig on GPIO23, Echo on GPIO24) to audio frequency from 220 Hz to 880 Hz, and control the volume (PWM duty cycle on GPIO18, PWM0) using a photoresistor (LDR) read via an MCP3008 ADC over SPI0. Handle sensor read errors, such as timeouts and SPI failures, gracefully by holding the last valid state, manage all resources cleanly on SIGINT, and save and load calibration data to 'theremin_config.txt'.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Honeywell AWM720P airflow sensor using its analog voltage output via an MCP3008 ADC (SPI channel 0, CE0, 1 MHz), using the pigpio library (not wiringPi) for SPI and a pigpio timer. The sensor outputs 0.5V at 0 SLPM and 4.5V at 200 SLPM (linear); sample the voltage every 100 ms and convert to airflow in SLPM using airflow = (voltage - 0.5) / (4.5 - 0.5) * 200. On SIGINT (Ctrl+C), close the SPI handle, close the log file, and terminate pigpio. The program should run indefinitely until interrupted.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using libgpiod v2 and spidev to sample analog audio from an ADMP401 MEMS microphone via a 10-bit MCP3008 SPI ADC. The ADMP401 analog output connects to MCP3008 CH0 (pin 1). Wiring: CS to GPIO8 (CE0, physical pin 24), MOSI to GPIO10 (physical pin 19), MISO to GPIO9 (physical pin 21), SCLK to GPIO11 (physical pin 23), VDD to 3.3V, VREF to 3.3V. Use /dev/spidev0.0 at SPI mode 0, 8 bits/word, 1 MHz max speed. Sample at 1000 Hz (1 ms period), sleeping until the next sample deadline with nanosleep. For each sample, manually control CS using libgpiod v2 (request GPIO8 as output, drive low before the transfer, high after), send the 3-byte MCP3008 single-ended channel-0 command (start bit 0x01, config byte (0x08|channel)<<4, dummy 0x00), and parse the 10-bit result from rx_buf[1..2]. Log each reading as "timestamp_ns|raw_adc_value\n" to 'audio_log.txt', using clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW) for nanosecond timestamps and flushing after each write.
